memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: If you make a vow to the Lord your God, do not be slow to pay it, for the Lord your God will certainly demand it of you and you will be guilty of sin. But if you refrain from making a vow, you will not be guilty. Whatever your lips utter you must be sure to do, because you made your vow freely to the Lord your God with your own mouth. - Deut 23:21-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God takes our words seriously, especially promises made to Him. If someone made a vow to the Lord, they were to fulfil it and not delay. Interestingly, God says there is no obligation to make a vow at all, but once you do, you are bound to keep it. Our promises to God are not to be made carelessly and then forgotten. What we freely commit with our mouths, we must faithfully carry out.

This teaches us the weight and value of our words. In a world where promises are broken easily and commitments treated lightly, God calls His people to integrity, to be those who mean what they say and keep their word. This is not about earning God's favour through vows, but about honouring Him with truthfulness and faithfulness.

Jesus taught His followers to be so honest and reliable that elaborate vows become unnecessary, our simple "yes" should mean yes, and our "no" should mean no (Matt 5:37). God is Himself perfectly faithful; He always keeps His promises, and He calls His people to reflect that faithfulness. When we make commitments, whether to God or to others, we honour Him by following through. Our reliability reflects the character of the God we serve. Are you a person whose word can be trusted? Is there a commitment you have made to God that you need to faithfully fulfil?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you a person whose word can be trusted?
2. Is there a commitment to God you need to fulfil?
3. How does God's faithfulness inspire your own?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are perfectly faithful and always keep Your word. Make me a person of integrity whose promises can be trusted, reflecting You. Amen.
